classInheritance.note: FieldService et al. derive from the bespoke MedDBase HubBase (a SignalR-style hub); methods are framework-invoked over the wire. F2 audit gap.
DataServer dispatches every concrete IServlet via ServletBase.Serve/Validate (IProfile). The abstract base is the dispatch join point. F2 audit gap.

Echo spawn<>/Router actors register a message handler conventionally named Inbox (passed as a method-group/lambda to Process.spawn). No shared base type to gate on, so match the name convention. ~93 sites. F4: added InstanceInbox (stateful spawn<S,T> handler); exact-name matching is brittle — a *Inbox suffix match would be more robust (deferred, needs rule-schema support).

Workflow masters are framework-invoked; RegisterEvents is the lifecycle hook that wires their BackgroundProcessSchedule timers (the timer delegates themselves are method-group handoffs â€” Layer-2, not rule-expressible).

BUG-rig-missed-entrypoints-healthcode: [ClientBinding] members (client-data-bound getters, invoked by the binding framework via reflection on render) are real user-triggered EPs but have no static caller. They live on non-ClientPage UI types (DetailDialogBase dialogs/panels), so the type rules skip them. baseTypes:* + the attribute gate (mirrors the WCF rule) catches the getter-enclosed ones (e.g. InvoiceHealthcodeSettingsDialog.get_InvoicePayeeOptions -> GetMedicalPerson/GetSite/GetCompany). EP detection is query-side; no re-index needed.

collapseSeams.label: reflection service-locator
collapseSeams.reason: ServiceHelper.CreateService constructs an IService by runtime string (assembly+type name from the ServiceStartupSet XML), so IService.Startup is a CHA fan-out to ALL ~113 IService impls. The runtime target is unknowable statically; expanding all of them buries the real call story (this one seam was ~92% of a depth-32 tree).

collapseSeams.label: charge-band pricing engine
collapseSeams.reason: BillingDataService.GetBillingData(2) is the entry to the charge-band / billing-rule pricing engine (~2.9k reachable methods: applicability rules, credit rules, LLBLGen fetch of ChargeBand/BillingRule). It is domain INFRASTRUCTURE re-entered from every price path (AddService, RefreshServicePrice, the panel rebuild) — the interesting question is almost always 'was a price resolved', not the engine internals. Folding to one summary leaf (union of effects + hidden count) keeps the price-fetch visible while stopping the engine from dominating every accounts tree. Render-only.

collapseSeams.label: service-list panel rebuild (re-prices every service)
collapseSeams.reason: ServiceListHelper.BuildServicesList is the wizard's UI-refresh hub: it rebuilds the whole PickServices panel and RE-RUNS the pricing engine for every chosen service, so it re-enters BillingDataService + the LLBLGen entity graph and alone accounts for ~4.8k of AddService's ~6.2k reachable methods. It is a rendering seam, not billing logic — the caller only cares that the panel refreshed. Folding it is the single biggest readability win for any accounts-wizard action tree. Render-only.

collapseSeams.label: entity cache fetch
collapseSeams.reason: The LLBLGen entity-instance cache factories — every *Cache.New / .NewEntity across MedDBase.DataAccessTier.EntityClasses (111) AND .EntityInstances (77): PersonCache, AccountCache, ServiceCache, ChargeBandCache, CompanyCache, ProfileCache, SiteCache, MpCache, … Each .New fetches-or-constructs a generated entity, fanning into <Entity>.New -> *EntityBase.InitClassFetch/InitClassMembers (throw-heavy field init) + a flood of get_* accessors. PersonCache.New alone reaches ~1.2k methods and is called from thousands of sites, so it re-explodes in every accounts/patient tree (folding it drops AddService's llm view ~3.2k->1.5k lines). Collapse (not opaque) keeps the effect UNION — entity_cache:read + the permission:assert from IfCanView + llblgen:fetch + the redis/echo cache-invalidation — on the summary leaf while hiding the construction subtree. The `*` wildcard ANCHORS the DataAccessTier namespace so the whole generated-cache family folds across BOTH namespaces while a same-named app cache elsewhere (e.g. MedDBase.ImportLayer2.Cache) is NOT caught.

opaqueTypes.label: Echo actor framework
opaqueTypes.reason: Echo.Process actor framework (spawn/tell/ask/fwd routing, ActorContext/ActorSystem/ActorDispatch* plumbing). The echo_publish:tell/ask EFFECT is attached at the app call site and still prints; descending into Echo's internal message routing is infrastructure noise. We have the source but rarely need to read it. (Echo.Process is being phased out per CLAUDE.md.) `M:` anchors to the declaring namespace so app methods that merely pass an Echo.ProcessId aren't matched.

opaqueTypes.label: LLBLGen ORM runtime
opaqueTypes.reason: LLBLGen ORM runtime (DataAccessAdapter/EntityBase2/collection/transaction support classes). The llblgen:read/write/fetch/tx EFFECTS attach at the app call site and still print; the adapter/support-class internals are ORM plumbing, not application logic.

opaqueTypes.label: LLBLGen entity init
opaqueTypes.reason: The LLBLGen-generated per-entity field-init plumbing — *EntityBase.InitClassFetch / InitClassMembers and *Entity.InitClassEmpty across MedDBase.DataAccessTier (671 occurrences in a single accounts tree, one per constructed entity type). Each is reached by CONCRETE ctor calls (<Entity>.#ctor -> base .#ctor -> InitClass*), NOT virtual fan-out, and its subtree is homogeneous plumbing: ~46 throw:raise field guards + a few assembly-load infra effects (lock/timer/io/reflection) + a single llblgen:read. The real DB fetch sits on the PARENT <Entity>.New, so opaque (keep own effects, drop the subtree) loses no signal — whereas collapse would surface the init-plumbing noise in a union chip. Opaque, sibling to the SD.LLBLGen.Pro. ORM-runtime rule (generated-entity side vs ORM-runtime side). Complementary to the entity-cache-fetch seam: that folds construction reached THROUGH a cache, this cleans up DIRECT new-XEntity / Entity.New construction. The `*` wildcard anchors DataAccessTier so app methods named InitClass* elsewhere aren't caught. Render-only.

opaqueTypes.label: perf logging
opaqueTypes.reason: MMS.Diagnostics perf-logging (PerformanceLogger/IPerformanceLogger/InMemory+Null impls + PerformanceLoggerExtensions). Many service methods wrap their body in PerformanceLogger.Factory.Log("area", "op", () => real work) — the wrapper resolves a logger via ClassFactory/MEF reflection and publishes timing to an Echo actor, dragging the actor framework + assembly-resolver plumbing (~290 methods) into the reach of anything perf-logged. The wrapped lambda (the REAL work) is a separate closure edge off the caller and still expands; only the logging arm is folded. Pure cross-cutting infrastructure.

opaqueTypes.label: LanguageExt functional lib
opaqueTypes.reason: LanguageExt functional library internals (Option/Either/Prelude/collection combinators). Pure plumbing reached via map/bind/match; almost never the thing being read.

opaqueTypes.label: MMS web UI framework
opaqueTypes.reason: MMS client-page web framework internals (ClientPage/ClientResponse/Actions.Helper request+render plumbing). The clientpage_proxy/nav/event/io EFFECTS are detected at the app page/proxy call site and still print; the framework's own internals are infrastructure.

opaqueTypes.label: typed service-locator interface
opaqueTypes.reason: IGenericServiceProvider is a pure locator facade (ProvideService<T>/ProvideService(string)) — the typed call resolves the real coupling on the RESULT via interface dispatch (single-impl), while the body is T-independent reflection construction over base IService (~113 impls). The ProvideService``1 method is already traversal-cut; this is render hygiene only, SCOPED TO THE INTERFACE (NOT the concrete providers ApplicationBase/Chamber/ApplicationNucleus, which carry real application logic). Render-only — opaque has zero graph/reachability effect (consumed only in TreeRenderer).

traversalCuts.label: reflection service-locator (CreateService)
traversalCuts.reason: ServiceHelper.CreateService constructs IService impls by runtime string (assembly+type from ServiceStartupSet XML). CHA fans it to ALL ~113 IService impls, exploding the tree and causing deep expansion to steal shallow calls (Task B). Cutting here stops the traversal before IService.Startup fan-out. --raw bypasses this cut.

traversalCuts.label: reflection service-locator (IService.Startup)
traversalCuts.reason: IService.Startup is CHA-fanned to ALL ~113 IService impls by the reflection service-locator. Cutting here (in addition to CreateService) ensures any path that reaches Startup directly is also stopped.

traversalCuts.label: typed service locator (ProvideService<T>)
traversalCuts.reason: ProvideService<T>() (declared on IGenericServiceProvider, Chamber, ApplicationNucleus and ApplicationBase) is the typed service-locator seam — its body fans through ServiceHelper.ProvideService -> CreateService -> IService.Startup (all ~113 impls), pure plumbing. The real coupling is the typed call on the RESULT (e.g. ProvideService<IReferralService>().GetDefaultReferralSummaryText), which already resolves to the concrete impl via interface dispatch on the receiver type — so the resolution is preserved while the locator drill-down is cut. Matching the generic method (``1) covers all four declaring types (the prior ApplicationBase substring missed Chamber/Nucleus/interface) and does not touch the ProvideServiceItem/ProvideServices import entities (no arity marker). --raw bypasses.

genericFactories.reason: Entity.New<TConstruct,TPk,TRecord>(pk) is the LLBLGen generic entity factory. The concrete construct type (type-arg 0, e.g. Account) fully determines the result, so the call-site edge is rewritten straight to <Construct>.New, bypassing the forwarding plumbing Entity.New``3 -> EntityCache`3.New -> ItemCache`3.Get -> Construct`2.New (which CHA-fans to every entity ctor). Collapses the tree to AccountCache.New -> Account.New and stops the fan-out from inflating the reach closure. Where the type arg is a forwarded parameter (not concrete) the edge is left for the in-memory generic-dispatch narrowing.
Entity.Find<TConstruct,TPk,TRecord> routes through the same Construct`2.New terminal as Entity.New (the construct's New(pk) overload), so it monomorphizes to <Construct>.New the same way.

contextDispatch.reason: A workflow Controller's State field (typed IWorkflowState) can only hold a state from its OWN family: every state derives from WorkflowStateBase<TController> naming its controller (e.g. AgedState : WorkflowStateBase<InvoiceDebtChase.Controller>). A naive dispatch of this.State.RegisterEvents()/UnRegisterEvents() fans to ALL ~14 IWorkflowState impls across unrelated workflows (PatientJourney, Referral, etc.). Narrowing to the enclosing controller's bound family (recovered from the WorkflowStateBase{C} base edge) drops the spurious cross-workflow subtrees while keeping the real one. Recall-safe: a dispatch carried without a known controller keeps the full fan-out.

effects.reason: redis_read: StackExchange.Redis read ops. Surfaces the distributed-store reads behind Echo ICluster/RedisClusterImpl that are otherwise invisible — the socket call lives in the external StackExchange.Redis lib, but the call SITE is first-party (e.g. RedisClusterImpl.GetHashField -> Db.HashGet).
redis_write: mutating ops (set/del/expire, list push/pop, db flush, batch/transaction). ListLeftPop is a destructive dequeue (write); FlushDatabase is destructive.
redis_publish: pub/sub publish (ISubscriber.Publish); captures the channel arg.

webhook_emit: IWebhooks.PublishEvent dispatches an OUTBOUND webhook (external side effect); captures the event-type arg. UX-panel gap (ux-research-2026-06 #1): this sink was invisible to `reaches --only http` on the document-save path (DocumentEntity.TriggerDocumentWebhook -> IWebhooks.PublishEvent), so an empty external-sink result read as 'safe'.

audit_write: AuditLog.Log()/TransactionalAuditLog.Log() (extension methods) commit an audit-log event — the .Log() terminating an AuditLog.Create(...) chain. UX-panel gap (ux-research-2026-06 #18): the 'every DB write preceded by an audit call' question was unanswerable because audit writes weren't modeled. Gated by the extension's declaring type, so it matches `auditLogEvent.Log()` and not the unrelated IAuditLog.Log(event) service form.

reflection_load: dynamic assembly load + instance creation by string name via the MMS ClassFactory service-locator (CreateInstance -> Assembly.Load/Assembly.CreateInstance, mms/MMS.Standard/ClassFactory.cs:82-109). A runtime code-loading boundary the call graph can't follow (the loaded type is a string). ~15 first-party sites.

config_read: MedDBase's custom MMS app-settings reads (IAppSettings.GetItem<T>/ContainsKey + the ConfigurationManager.GetItem<T> extension, mms/MMS.Standard/ConfigurationManager.cs:141). The built-in `config` rule targets BCL System.Configuration / Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration which this codebase does not use. The low-level appsettings boundary; the app-level IConfiguration family is tagged separately below. Captures the key (first arg).

config_read (app-level): IConfiguration.GetItem<T>/ContainsKey on the config readers (LoggedInProfile/Account/Application/Web/PersistentApplication). These read configuration[key] / web.config DIRECTLY — they do NOT all funnel through the low-level MMS appsettings anchor, so e.g. Settings.OpenAiKey surfaced as no config effect. Matched on the IConfiguration interface receiver (catches Global.Application.Configuration.GetItem) + the concrete config impls. Deliberately EXCLUDES the sibling IPersistentApplicationState impls (WebApplicationState/WebState) — those are application STATE, not config. Captures the key (first arg).

http_response_write: inbound ASP.NET response IO to the client (body/file/header/cookie/redirect). The `io` provider is file-only (System.IO.*) and `http` is OUTBOUND-only (HttpClient/WebClient) — so a raw IHttpHandler/HttpTaskAsyncHandler's entire response surface, including client document-download byte streams (e.g. PatientPortalHttpHandler.RespondWithDocumentDownload), produced zero effects. Anchored on HttpResponse(+Base) write methods. (Response.OutputStream.Write goes via System.IO.Stream and is not caught here — accepted; the direct HttpResponse write methods cover the meaningful sites.)

llblgen_collection_read: EntityCollectionBase`1 (SelfServicing, the base MedDBase actually uses) was missing from this gate while EntityCollectionBase2 (Adapter) was present. It is also the m:n NAVIGATION-LOAD boundary — the generated `PerformMultiEntityLazyLoading(..., (c,r)=>c.GetMulti(filter,r))` lambda in every EntityBase is a real per-navigation SELECT, and `c` is the TYPED collection so receiver_type names the entity. Note the gate is equality-or-dotted-prefix, so this entry does NOT also swallow EntityCollectionBase2.

llblgen_navigation_load_many_to_one: the m:1 / 1:n half of the generated lazy-load surface. `XxxEntityBase.GetMultiYyy(...)` bottoms out in `PerformMultiEntityLazyLoading(..., (c,r)=>c.GetMultiManyToOne(this,null,filter))` — a real SELECT per navigation touch. The name is LLBLGen-generated and appears on nothing else: all 347 declaring types in this store end in `Collection` and live under a `*.DataAccessTier.CollectionClasses` namespace, so the name-suffix gate is tight without pinning a namespace list (Labs/Pathways/PaymentGateway each have their own). Declaring type and receiver both name the entity collection; receiver_type is used for symmetry with llblgen_collection_read. The m:n half needs no rule of its own — those trampolines call EntityCollectionBase`1.GetMulti, which that rule now covers.

entity_generic_factory_read: Entity.New<TConstruct,TPk,TRecord>/Find<..> is the generic entity factory; the method signature pins the constructed entity to type-arg position 0, so typeArgumentIndex:0 resolves the effect to that one type at the concrete call site (entity_cache:read Account) instead of the CHA-fanned per-entity Construct`2.New aggregate. declaringTypes gate is exactly the base `Entity` type (StartsWith(gate+'.') excludes EntityClasses.*).

permission_check_arg1: the Rights.* right is argument 1 for HasRight(pkCert, right, txn, profileId) / HasAccountRight(accountId, right, ...) / HasAnyRight(pkCert, mask, ...). argument_name yields the named right (Rights.Account.CanViewAccounts). NOTE: the rarer HasRight(pkCert, profileId, right, txn) overload puts the right at arg 2 and will mis-index here — validate frequency against the store.
permission_assert_arg2: AssertRight(recordKey, pkCertificate, rightToAssert, ...) — the throwing variant; right is argument 2.
permission_chamber_arg0: HasChamberRight(Rights.Company right, ...) / AssertChamberRight(Rights.Company right, ...) — the right is argument 0.
languageext_parallel_traverse: SequenceParallel/TraverseParallel runs the traversed effects across threads (windowed) — concurrency the linear call graph otherwise hides.

bounded_retry: a config-gated RetryCount/RetryLimit read that bounds an actor re-tell (OrderRequestForAppointmentMsg.Retry). The Inbox handler reads RetryCount (config-backed, ProcessConfig.read) and only re-tells the Retry message while msg.Attempts <= RetryCount (OrderRequestForAppointment.cs:123,129). A config change to that bound (e.g. raising/lowering the cap, or removing the guard) is INVISIBLE to the effect-SET diff — the actor:tell is present either way — but is behaviorally significant (it changes the re-delivery loop bound). Surfacing the RetryCount read as its own derived effect makes that change appear in `impact` (a +/- bounded_retry:guard, or an amplification if it moves). SCOPE NOTE: this is the schema-supported APPROXIMATION of the intended observation 'a RetryCount read reached on the path BEFORE a Retry re-tell'. The observation rule schema (resilienceRetry/concurrencyHandled/resourceSpan/readBeforeCommit) keys ONLY off the lexical structural context of a single effect's own enclosing method (its enclosing invocations / catch types / scopes / loop), so it CANNOT express a cross-method path/guarding relationship; the read and the Retry tell live in different methods linked only by the call path. Narrowly gated to the OrderRequestForAppointment declaring type (not generalized to arbitrary config-gated control flow) to avoid matching the unrelated DatabaseMaxRetryCount / EntityField.RetryCount / NotifyClientMessage.RetryCount sites.

staticInitCapture._doc: static_init_capture (GI-862 class): a config/feature-flag value read inside a STATIC field initializer runs once at CLR type-init and never re-evaluates — stale until app restart. Flags an effect reading a mutableSources resource whose enclosing symbol is a static field. Disclosed candidate (medium); some hits are benign deploy-time-constant flags. mutableSources = resource substring patterns that count as a mutable/config source.

observations._doc: amplification WIDENING (concats with the builtin network-first scope): entity_cache reads join the displayed amplification tier. Rationale (2026-08-04): per-entity caches ARE the DB-read mask in this codebase — every ProfileCache.New/AccountCache.New in a loop is a cold-key DB fetch per distinct element, and prod's worst per-trace offender (PROFILE, 11,461 SELECTs in one trace) flows exactly through this shape (Home2.cs GetProfilesAndActiveLicenses). A looped entity_cache read is therefore a network-amplification claim, not an in-proc detail.

crossMethodAmplification._doc: cross_method_amplification — presence-join(iteration_fanout, witness, fwd-tree<=maxDepth): a gated effect reachable AT OR BENEATH a call issued once per element (the lexical n_plus_1 cannot see it — the iteration context and the effect live in different frames). N+1 is just the read subset; sends/publishes/writes amplify identically, so the gate is ALL-IO: `witnesses` omitted = every effect provider except excludeWitnessProviders (engine default: alloc, throw, shared_state, config — intrinsic/memory, never an IO round trip). Widened from the original read-only gate 2026-08-04 after the hotspot triage showed looped SENDS (echo/queue/smtp/http:POST) were structurally invisible. maxDepth 6 is the measured recall knee and a RESOURCE bound, not a semantic gate — depth is emitted as data. maxWitnessesPerAnchor 1 = nearest-depth finding grain (0 = the full anchor x witness cross product for analysis runs).

cacheCoherence._doc: FR-7 cache-coherence correlation (effect-correlation reframe). An llblgen:bulk_write to a cached entity whose forward closure has no same-entity cache:invalidate is flagged. cachedEntities = the DECLARED contract (high confidence — still flags if every invalidation is deleted); entities merely READ from cache (entity_cache:read) are discovered automatically at medium confidence. excludeEnclosingNamespaceSuffix drops the generated LLBLGen cascade mutators (CollectionClasses/DaoClasses) that are never the real bug site.

files._experiment: Option-3: NO generated-file exclusions — index LLBLGen generated boilerplate too, to measure the cost (store/graph size, index time) vs the noise/perf rationale for excluding it.

projects._reason: Tests, DACPAC models, and build tooling only — NEVER production libraries. `dfs` and `MMS.Net` sat here from the 2026-05-28 init with no recorded reason; that silently blinded every trace into MedDBase.DistributedFileService (effects still tagged at call sites via receiverTypes, so the store LOOKED complete) until 2026-07-15.
